name: Sip
summary: Monitors capacitive soil hydration levels and automatically dispenses precise water doses using a 5V submersible pump via an isolated relay, showing live soil moisture % and status on an OLED display.

parts.name: Arduino Uno R3
parts.why: Main control unit executing sensor polling loop, threshold decision logic, and OLED rendering

parts.name: Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensor v1.2
parts.why: Corrosion-resistant analog probe providing continuous soil volumetric water content measurements

parts.name: 5V 1-Channel Relay Module
parts.why: Electrically isolates the microcontroller while switching high inrush current to the DC pump

parts.name: Mini DC Submersible Water Pump 3-6V
parts.why: Pumps water from reservoir through silicone tubing directly into plant soil

parts.name: 0.96 inch I2C OLED Display (SSD1306)
parts.why: Shows real-time moisture gauge, pump state, and diagnostic readings

parts.name: 5V 2A Regulated Power Supply
parts.why: Supplies stable current for Uno and handles pump startup transients without brownouts

Affordable ₹1,285 bill of materials with standard off-the-shelf maker components

buildSteps: Step 1: 3D print the enclosure base and snap lid in PLA or PETG with 20% infill and 0.2mm layer height.
Step 2: Mount the Arduino Uno board into the base posts using four M3x6mm screws.
Step 3: Secure the 5V relay module into the right chassis cradle and route the control wire to pin D7.
Step 4: Snap the 0.96-inch SSD1306 OLED display into the upper lid bezel and connect I2C pins (SDA to A4, SCL to A5).
Step 5: Connect the capacitive moisture probe to 5V, GND, and analog input pin A0 using the silicone grommet pass-through.
Step 6: Connect the 5V mini pump to the relay normally-open (NO) terminal and feed the inlet tube into your water reservoir.
Step 7: Connect 5V 2A power to the DC barrel jack, insert the probe into your plant soil, and watch Sip automatically hydrate your plant.
